question: Does the 2015-2018 Lake Taal early-life-stage study supply species-level evidence for the CALABARZON baseline, and what is its valid role?

study.method: One 10-minute subsurface horizontal plankton-net tow at each station during an approximately 11-hour night sampling period; larval fish were morphologically identified only to family.

assessment.validUse: Historical lake-wide, family-level early-life-stage ecology and environmental context; it documents multi-year sampling effort and a family-level composition signal.
notSupported: No larval fish was identified to species in the study, so the family observations cannot validate any species-level Lake Taal occurrence or named-fish spawning claim.
The 2015-2018 study does not establish 2026 presence, a current fish population, adult distribution or a complete Lake Taal species list.
Eggs are not taxonomically assigned in the paper.
The authors proposed possible spawning/larval foraging areas for protection, but the article does not itself establish a current legal fishing closure or authoritative boundary.
The article is not a fish diet or bait source and does not establish present water safety or fishing permission.
assessment.geography: The paper names 12 georeferenced Lake Taal stations and provides coordinates in an appendix. They were not copied, converted or used as species occurrence points or app geometry in this review.
assessment.relevanceToCoveragePlan: This adds a historical inland-lake study to the L1 CALABARZON research base, but it does not advance the species-level baseline to complete. Continue looking for station- and taxon-resolved evidence while keeping freshwater, brackish and marine source lanes distinct.

accessAndReuse.officialPdfReader: Full publisher PDF text was accessible through the web reader/search representation.
accessAndReuse.license: No item-specific reuse license was verified in the article text or publisher record.
accessAndReuse.disposition: No PDF bytes, tables, figures, station coordinates, monthly data or copied text were stored in the project. No publication approval.

nextAction: National rollout step 397: continue the L1 CALABARZON inland-water sweep with a primary source that identifies fish to species and ties each name to a dated lake, river or reach. Keep this Taal study as family-level historical ecological context only; do not infer species identities or current legal zones.
